title: Monarch Butterfly Count Nears 30-Year Low
titleZh: 帝王蝶数量逼近30年低点
credits: Todd Richmond reported this story for the Associated Press. Jill Robbins adapted it for Learning English.

sentences.en: An American nonprofit group says the number of monarch butterflies spending the winter in the western United States has dropped to its second-lowest mark in nearly 30 years.
sentences.zh: 一家美国非营利组织表示，在美国西部越冬的帝王蝶数量已降至近30年来的第二低点。

sentences.en: The Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation, based in Oregon, said the causes for this include the use of chemicals to kill insects, known as pesticides.
sentences.zh: 总部位于俄勒冈州的无脊椎动物保护协会泽尔西斯学会表示，造成这一情况的原因包括使用被称为农药的化学物质来消灭昆虫。

sentences.en: The group also blames reductions in habitat and climate change.
sentences.zh: 该组织还将栖息地的减少和气候变化归咎于相关因素。

sentences.en: Monarch butterflies are known for their clear orange-and-black markings.
sentences.zh: 帝王蝶以其鲜明的橙黑相间斑纹而闻名。

sentences.en: They live across North America.
sentences.zh: 它们分布于北美各地。

sentences.en: Monarchs in the eastern United States spend the winter in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 美国东部的帝王蝶在墨西哥越冬。

sentences.en: The World Wildlife Fund, a non-profit based in Switzerland, counts them there but has not yet released data for this year.
sentences.zh: 总部位于瑞士的世界自然基金会已在当地对它们进行了统计，但尚未公布今年的数据。

sentences.en: Monarchs west of the Rocky Mountains usually spend the winter along the California coast.
sentences.zh: 落基山脉西面的帝王蝶通常在美国加利福尼亚州沿海地区越冬。

sentences.en: The Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation has been counting western overwinter populations in California and Arizona for the last 28 years.
sentences.zh: 泽尔西斯学会已在过去28年间对加利福尼亚州和亚利桑那州的西部越冬种群进行了统计。

sentences.en: The highest number recorded was 1.2 million in 1997.
sentences.zh: 有记录以来的最高数量为1997年的120万只。

sentences.en: The organization announced Friday that it counted just 9,119 monarchs in 2024, a decrease of 96 percent from 233,394 in 2023.
sentences.zh: 该组织周五宣布，2024年他们统计到的帝王蝶仅有9119只，比2023年的233394只减少了96%。

sentences.en: The total was the second lowest since the survey began in 1997.
sentences.zh: 这一总数是自1997年开展调查以来的第二低水平。

sentences.en: The record-low count was 1,901 monarchs in 2020.
sentences.zh: 有记录以来的最低数量为2020年的1901只。

sentences.en: The survey noted that a place in Santa Barbara that saw 33,200 monarchs last winter had only 198 butterflies this year.
sentences.zh: 该调查指出，去年冬季曾有33200只帝王蝶出没的圣巴巴拉一处地区，今年仅有198只。

sentences.en: Monarchs across North America face increasing threats.
sentences.zh: 北美各地的帝王蝶正面临日益增加的威胁。

sentences.en: One is the supply of a plant, milkweed, which they feed on as caterpillars.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是它们作为幼虫所依赖的一种植物马利筋的供应。

sentences.en: Monarch Joint Venture is a nonprofit group based in Minnesota that aims to protect monarchs.
sentences.zh: 帝王蝶联合保护组织是一家总部位于明尼苏达州的非营利组织，旨在保护帝王蝶。

sentences.en: The group said milkweed has been disappearing because of dry weather, wildfires, agriculture and urban development.
sentences.zh: 该组织表示，由于天气干旱、野火、农业和城市开发，马利筋正在消失。

sentences.en: The Xerces Society said pesticides might be on the remaining plants.
sentences.zh: 泽尔西斯学会表示，农药可能残留在现存的马利筋植株上。

sentences.en: Emma Pelton is a biologist with the Xerces Society.
sentences.zh: 艾玛·佩尔顿是泽尔西斯学会的一名生物学家。

sentences.en: She said it is unclear what caused such a sharp decrease in the western population in just one year.
sentences.zh: 她说，目前尚不清楚是什么导致了西部种群仅用一年时间就出现了如此剧烈的下降。

sentences.en: The monarch population is already small, she said, and heat above 37.7 degrees Celsius in the western states last year might have slowed breeding.
sentences.zh: 她说，帝王蝶种群数量本来就很少，去年西部各州气温超过37.7摄氏度可能减缓了它们的繁殖。

sentences.en: Monarchs suffer when the temperature gets up to 37.7 degrees Celsius and any temperatures above 42.2 degrees Celsius will kill the insects, Pelton said.
sentences.zh: 佩尔顿说，当气温升至37.7摄氏度时，帝王蝶就会受苦，而任何超过42.2摄氏度的气温都会杀死这些昆虫。

sentences.en: The western states saw a heat wave in July with temperatures in some areas well past 37.7 degrees.
sentences.zh: 西部各州在7月经历了一波热浪，部分地区气温远超37.7摄氏度。

sentences.en: Palm Springs, for example, reportedly reached a record 51.1 degrees Celsius on July 5.
sentences.zh: 据报道，棕榈泉在7月5日达到了创纪录的51.1摄氏度。

sentences.en: Another heat wave hit northern California in early October, with several cities breaking heat records.
sentences.zh: 10月初，另一波热浪袭击了加利福尼亚州北部，多座城市打破了高温纪录。

sentences.en: Pelton said that it is too early to tell what long-term effect the sharp drop might have on the overall western monarch population.
sentences.zh: 佩尔顿说，现在判断这种骤降对西部帝王蝶总体的长期影响还为时过早。

sentences.en: Insects can reproduce very quickly, Pelton said.
sentences.zh: 佩尔顿说，昆虫可以非常快速地繁殖。

sentences.en: After a low point of 1,901 butterflies in 2020, the population recovered to 247,246 insects the following year, an increase of nearly 13,000 percent.
sentences.zh: 在2020年降至1901只的低点后，种群数量在次年恢复到247246只，增长了近13000%。

sentences.en: The year after that the survey recorded 335,479 monarchs.
sentences.zh: 再下一年，调查记录了335479只帝王蝶。

sentences.en: "This is bad news," Pelton said of the 2024 population drop.
sentences.zh: 佩尔顿谈到2024年种群数量下降时说：'这是坏消息。'

sentences.en: "But we have seen incredible recovery.
sentences.zh: '但我们已经看到了惊人的恢复。

sentences.en: This doesn't mean we're not going to have western monarchs.”
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们不会再有帝王蝶。'

sentences.en: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service announced in December 2024 that it wanted to list monarchs as threatened.
sentences.zh: 美国鱼类和野生动物管理局在2024年12月宣布，希望将帝王蝶列为受威胁物种。

sentences.en: Such a move would ban people from killing or transporting them.
sentences.zh: 此举将禁止人们杀死或运输它们。

sentences.en: The proposed change would also ban property owners from making changes to their property that would make it unusable to the butterflies.
sentences.zh: 拟议中的变更还将禁止财产所有者对其财产进行改动，从而使其无法供蝶类使用。

sentences.en: For example, removing all milkweed from a property would by banned by law.
sentences.zh: 例如，清除财产上的所有马利筋将被法律禁止。

sentences.en: Earthjustice is an environmental nonprofit legal group based in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 地球正义是一个总部位于旧金山的环境非营利法律组织。

sentences.en: It asked the Environmental Protection Agency in December 2024 to require testing of pesticides’ effects on insects such as bees, moths and butterflies.
sentences.zh: 它在2024年12月要求美国环境保护局要求对农药蜜蜂、蛾子和蝶类等昆虫的影响进行测试。

sentences.en: I’m Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

glossary.def: a chemical that is used to kill animals or insects that damage plants or crops
the place or environment where a living thing lives
a study of a subject aimed at finding something out
an early stage in the life of certain insects
to produce young animals, birds, or the like
